    AI Overview
    Lehigh University consistently ranks among top national universities, often around the #40-50 range in U.S. News & World Report for National Universities (e.g., #46 for 2026) and performs strongly in value and career outcomes, appearing in the top 15 for salary impact in The Wall Street Journal rankings and top 20 for long-term career success on LinkedIn. It's also recognized as an R1 top-tier research institution by Carnegie. 
    Key Rankings & Recognition:
    • U.S. News & World Report (2026): #46 National Universities, #24 Best Value Schools. 
    • The Wall Street Journal (2025/2026): #15 Best Colleges, recognized for strong salary impact and graduation rates. 
    • LinkedIn: #17 Top Colleges for Long-Term Career Success. 
    • Times Higher Education (THE) (2026): Ranks in various subject areas globally, including #601-800 for World University Rankings. 
    • Carnegie Classification: Designated as a top-tier R1 research university. 
    Factors in its Rankings:
    • Career Success: High marks for graduate earnings and career growth, fueled by strong alumni networks and programs. 
    • Value: Strong performance in "Best Value" categories, indicating good return on investment. 
    • Research: Classified as a leading research institution (R1). 
    Note: Rankings can vary by publication and year, but Lehigh consistently appears as a highly-ranked private university with strong career outcomes.

      Admission Requirements. What are the admission requirements for Lehigh University?
      About this result
      Feedback
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Lehigh University seeks top students with strong academics (near straight A's, challenging courses like AP/IB), requiring transcripts, recommendations, essays, and activities, with deadlines for Early Decision (Nov 1) & Regular Decision (Jan 1). They are test-optional, but competitive scores are around 1350-1490 SAT or 31-33 ACT if submitted, with specific English proficiency tests (TOEFL/IELTS) needed for international applicants.
       
      First-Year Undergraduate Requirements
      • Application: Submit via Common App. 
      • Deadlines: Early Decision I (Nov 1), Early Decision II (Jan 1), Regular Decision (Jan 1). 
      • Materials: Transcripts, essays, personal qualities, activities, and leadership descriptions.
      • Recommendations: Letters of recommendation are required. 
      • Testing: Test-optional (SAT/ACT), but scores help if submitted (Middle 50%: 1400-1510 SAT / 32-34 ACT). 
      • Application Fee: $75 (waivers available). 
      International Applicants
      • English Proficiency: Required if English isn't your first language, with scores like TOEFL (above 90), IELTS (7.0), or Duolingo (110+).
      • Exceptions: Granted if you've completed your last two years of schooling in English. 
      Graduate Admissions (Varies by Program)
      • General: Transcripts, 2-3 recommendations, resume, statement of purpose, fee. 
      • Example (Political Science): Rolling admissions, GRE optional, priority for funding due March 1. 
      • Example (Engineering): Minimum GPA requirements (e.g., 2.75 undergrad for M.Eng. in TE), with specific criteria varying by program.

        Athletics. What are the athletic programs at Lehigh University?
        About this result
        Feedback
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Lehigh University offers a comprehensive NCAA Division I athletic program (the Mountain Hawks) within the Patriot League, featuring 12 men's and 12 women's varsity teams like basketball, soccer, lacrosse, swimming, and track & field, alongside popular club sports such as rugby, cycling, and equestrian, all supporting student leadership, teamwork, and competitive athletics.
         
        Varsity Sports (NCAA Division I)
        Lehigh sponsors a wide array of sports for both men and women, including:
        • Men's:
          Baseball, Basketball, Cross Country, Football, Golf, Lacrosse, Rowing, Soccer, Swimming & Diving, Tennis, Track & Field, Wrestling. 
        • Women's:
          Basketball, Cross Country, Field Hockey, Golf, Lacrosse, Rowing, Soccer, Softball, Swimming & Diving, Tennis, Track & Field, Volleyball. 
        Club Sports
        For students seeking other athletic outlets, Lehigh offers numerous club sports, including: 
        • Equestrian, Flag Football, Gymnastics, Indoor Soccer, Rugby, Cycling, Water Polo, and more.
        Athletic Identity 
        • Nickname: Mountain Hawks.
        • Conference: Patriot League (NCAA Division I).
        • Football: Competes in the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS).

          Description

          Lehigh University is a private research university in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, United States. The university was established in 1865 by businessman Asa Packer. Lehigh University's undergraduate programs have been coeducational since the 1971–72 academic year. Wikipedia

          Mascot: Clutch the Mountain Hawk
          Typical SAT scores: Reading and Writing 680-730, Math 690-770 (2023–24) IPEDS
          Colors: Brown and white;
          Endowment: $2 billion (2025)
